fullPassage:
The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal.

(B) The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system.

(A) However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world.

(C) Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports.

questions.passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to ①<u>achieving</u> food security and a wide variety of mechanisms ②<u>has been developed</u> to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of ③<u>insuring</u> that adequate amounts of food ④<u>are</u> available to the resident population.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② has been developed → have been developed: 주어 mechanisms가 복수이므로 have.
det.analysis:
✅ ① achieving: 전치사 to 뒤 동명사, 적절
❌ ② has: mechanisms(복수) → have been developed
✅ ③ insuring: 전치사 of 뒤 동명사, 적절
✅ ④ are: amounts(복수), 적절
det.tip: 주어-동사 수일치: 복수 주어 → have (not has)

questions.passage: Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, ①<u>which</u> means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily ②<u>producing</u> within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly ③<u>sensitive</u> to climatic, soil and other conditions that ④<u>tend</u> to vary around the world.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② producing → produced: food items는 '생산되는' 대상이므로 과거분사 수동.
det.analysis:
✅ ① which: 관계대명사, 적절
❌ ② producing: items는 생산의 대상 → produced
✅ ③ sensitive: be + 형용사, 적절
✅ ④ tend: conditions that tend, 적절
det.tip: 능동 ~ing vs 수동 p.p.: items produced(생산된)

questions.passage: Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, ①<u>depends</u> on imports for ②<u>its</u> supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of ③<u>assure</u> adequate food supplies is solved by ④<u>relying</u> on both domestic production and imports.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ assure → assuring: the problem of 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① depends: The United States(단수), 적절
✅ ② its: The United States의 소유격, 적절
❌ ③ assure: of + 동명사 → assuring
✅ ④ relying: by + 동명사, 적절

det.korean: ③ export(수출) → import(수입): 국내 생산 어려운 품목은 '수입'해야 함.
det.analysis:

✅ ② adequate: 원문 그대로
❌ ③ export: 원문은 import → export로 바뀌어 부적절
✅ ④ sensitive: 원문 그대로

Agricultural products are highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to ②<u>remain constant</u> around the world. Even countries with extremely ③<u>productive</u> agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient. In general, the problem is solved by ④<u>relying</u> on both domestic production and imports.

det.korean: ② remain constant(일정하다) → vary(다양하다): 조건은 세계적으로 '다양'하다.
det.analysis:

❌ ② remain constant: 원문은 vary(다양하다)
✅ ③ productive: 원문 그대로
✅ ④ relying: 원문 그대로

reducing the variety of available food items

det.korean: 빈칸: 국내 생산과 수입 둘 다에 의존하는 것이 해결책.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ relying on both: 원문 결론과 일치
❌ ① complete self-sufficiency: 불필요하다고 했음
❌ ② eliminating imports: 반대 방향
❌ ③ reducing variety: 언급 없음
det.tip: both A and B = A와 B 둘 다

questions.passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: every country has already achieved food self-sufficiency
food security does not require food self-sufficiency
agricultural products are resistant to climate change
all countries must eliminate food imports entirely

det.korean: However(역접) 뒤: 자급자족이 필수가 아니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② food security does not require: However 역접 + 핵심 주장
❌ ① already achieved: 이미 달성했다는 내용 없음
❌ ③ resistant: sensitive가 맞음
❌ ④ eliminate imports: 반대
det.tip: However = 역접. 앞의 자급자족 → 뒤에서 반박

questions.passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

소수의 나라만 식량 안보에 관심을 가진다.
식량 안보의 첫 번째 문제는 수출 확대이다.

❌ ② 아직 개발되지 않음: have been developed(개발됨)
❌ ③ 소수: virtually every(거의 모든)
❌ ④ 수출 확대: 식량 확보(available)가 문제

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

극도로 생산적인 농업 부문을 가진 나라도 완전한 자급자족은 어렵다.
모든 나라는 국내에서 모든 식품을 생산할 수 있다.

det.korean: 원문: Even countries with extremely productive sectors are not fully self-sufficient.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 완전한 자급자족 어려움: 원문 일치
❌ ① 반드시: does not require
❌ ② 영향 안 받음: highly sensitive
❌ ④ 모든 식품 생산: not fully self-sufficient

questions.passage: The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

미국은 모든 식품을 국내에서 자체 생산한다.

det.analysis:
✅ ① 커피 수입: 원문 일치
✅ ② 바나나 수입: 원문 일치
✅ ③ 병행 해결: 원문 일치
❌ ④ 모든 식품 자체 생산: depends on imports와 불일치
